bull_bear.body:
- 'Net Debt to Equity at 0.29x vs 0.26x at March 2026, comfortable headroom for incremental borrowings to fund future growth opportunities'; the debt-profile chart shows Gross Debt rising Rs. 193 Cr (Jun 30, 2025) to Rs. 581 Cr (Jun 30, 2026) and Net Debt from Rs. -50 Cr to Rs. 215 Cr, with Net Debt to Equity of (0.08x), (0.05x), 0.13x, 0.26x, 0.29x over the same five quarter-ends.
- Borrowing cost has trended down across the five quarter-ends from 10.1% (Jun 30, 2025) to 9.4% (Jun 30, 2026).
- Cash generation is being recycled into land rather than distributed: FY26 Net Operating Cashflow Rs. 417 Cr and Q1 FY27 Rs. 81 Cr, against Net Investing Cashflow of Rs. (638) Cr in FY26 and Rs. (225) Cr in Q1 FY27; Loans/OCD drawdown (net) was Rs. 320 Cr in FY26 and Rs. 224 Cr in Q1 FY27.
- Dividend Payment of Rs. (25) Cr is shown for FY26 and nil for Q1 FY27; 'Pref Issue / Equity' shows Rs. (19) Cr for FY26 and nil for Q1 FY27.
- Platform funding from HDFC Capital Advisors: a 'Rs. 900 Cr residential development platform with HDFC Capital Advisors', a 'Strategic partnership with HDFC Capital Advisors for long term platform funding', and a 'Preferential issue of Rs. 85 Cr to HDFC Capital Advisors (8.8% on fully diluted basis) and Promoters', plus 'Infusion of funds by Promoter and Promoter Group'.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Part of 'THE LALBHAI GROUP', described as 'A USD ~3 billion diversified enterprise with a strong presence across four key growth sectors of the Indian economy', spanning Fashion and Retail, Real Estate and Engineering, with a legacy traced to 1897 and Arvind Mill (1931) 'now demerged in to four listed entities'.
- 'COMPANY HISTORY - OPERATING SINCE 2008'; listed on NSE and BSE through demerger from Arvind Limited (2015 on the journey timeline), entering the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Vadodara, Gujarat in later years.
- Focused geographies are Gujarat, Bengaluru and MMR, under a 'NICHE RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT MODEL' that is 'RESIDENTIAL FOCUSED'; the June 2026 project classification of ongoing and planned projects shows Residential at 92% against a Commercial/Industrial category.
- Long term credit rating: 'AA-/Stable Rated by India Ratings & Research (Upgraded to AA-/Stable from A+/Stable in June 2026).'
- Awards cited for FY 2026 include 'Developer of the Year - Residential' at the 17th Realty Conclave & Excellence Awards 2025, and Township / Iconic project of the Year for Arvind Aquacity.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Visibility] Unrecognized Revenue stands at Rs. 3,825 Cr as on 30 Jun 2026 vs Rs. 3,733 Cr at Mar 31, 2026, having risen from Rs. 1,506 Cr as on 31 Mar 23.
- [Cashflow runway] The estimated-operating-cashflow table shows Grand Total Est. Operating Cashflow of Rs. 5,335 Cr, less 'Add: Surplus/(Deficit) -215', giving 'Net Estimated Unrealised Operating Cashflow' of Rs. 5,119 Cr; state splits are Gujarat Rs. 2,333 Cr, Karnataka Rs. 2,104 Cr and Maharashtra Rs. 898 Cr.
- [Leadership] Board chaired by Kulin S. Lalbhai (Non-Executive Director) with Priyansh Kapoor as Managing Director & CEO, Kamal Singal as Whole Time Director - Strategy & Investments, and Vipul Roongta as Nominee Director; the senior management page shows a largely newly assembled team, with the COO, CFO, Head - Business Development and Head - Strategy all 'With ASL since 2025' and the CBO-South and Head-Legal since 2026.
- [Governance/consistency] The safe harbor states the presentation 'is based on the publicly available information including but not limited to Company's website and Annual Reports.'

deepdive.thesis: Arvind SmartSpaces is well-positioned to benefit from the growing demand for residential real estate in India, driven by its strong brand, execution capabilities, and strategic expansion across key growth markets. The company's focus on building a diversified portfolio, deepening city-level operating structures, and maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation will drive long-term growth and value creation for shareholders.
